resolution_note: Built-in source is 1254 square. Runtime albedo is resampled, not native generated 4K. User declined API fallback.
prompts:
Edit the provided rock-face photograph into a production game texture. Deliver a 4K 4096 x 4096 pixel square image with genuinely resolved fine photographic mineral and fracture detail. The user's requested visual is THIS reference's dense rough layers and irregular dark mineral patches, brighter because the reference is in shadow.

Fill the square with an orthographic front-facing expanse of this Grand Canyon rock, zoomed out to cover roughly 90m width and 180m height in its eventual UV mapping: dozens of thin beds, uneven broken shelves, multiple thicker beds subdivided by closely spaced horizontal laminations, vertical joints and small blocks. Preserve the distinctly irregular dark gray-brown weathering/varnish contrasting against dusty warm rose-brown exposed sandstone, tiny buff mineral flecks, ragged eroded chips, fine fissures and granular mottling. Rich local COLOR detail throughout the rock, not a monotone brown material, not just embossed grooves. Irregular groupings and interrupted bands with nonuniform thicknesses. Alternate dark stained crust with brighter exposed patches, no evenly repeated stripes. No big blank slabs.

Relight to bright neutral diffuse daylight: lift the shadowed reference's overall exposure substantially but retain its strong local contrast and dense detail. Moderate its saturated burnt orange/red toward dusty rose, light brown and neutral sandstone beige so satellite imagery can determine the overall terrain color. No green tint, no oversaturated orange. No directional sunlight, cast shadow, highlights or haze baked in. Remove vegetation and landscape perspective. Continuous rock fills the entire image, no sky, horizon, sloping landscape, ground plane, borders or text. Seamlessly tileable on all four edges. Sharp high resolution photographic PBR albedo, not painted, smooth, soft, blurred or stylized. Output only this one 4096x4096 texture.

Edit image 1, the current game cliff texture. Image 2 is geological reference. Critical correction: image 1 has uniformly scattered dark mottling everywhere. Replace that with DISTINCT STRATIGRAPHIC LAYERS that change visibly up and down the image. Dark material must be concentrated in certain specific beds, not distributed uniformly through every layer.

Make a square orthographic seamless sedimentary cliff albedo, zoomed-out detailed rock surface. At least seven visibly different geological intervals of UNEQUAL thickness across the vertical dimension. Examples of the desired sequence and variation: pale buff/gray-beige thin shale laminations; a narrow dark brown weathered resistant bed; a thicker dusty rose fractured sandstone interval with mostly clean light stone and only sparse stains; numerous delicate pale and russet laminae; a distinct substantial muted gray-brown varnished bed with dark blocky faces; a thick warmer light rose-brown bed with vertical jointing and very little dark mottling; an interval of many fine beige/rust layers. Use this as geological variation, not a rigid diagram. Irregular eroded contacts, interruptions, thin lenses, subtle gentle changes in bed thickness along width, diverse small fractures and fine mineral flecks within each layer. Layers predominantly horizontal, continuous enough to read as real stratigraphy. Change both color AND texture by interval: massive fractured sandstone versus thin crumbly laminated beds. Do not distribute the same dark-speckle texture evenly over all layers. No identical repeated stripes or masonry. No large smooth blank regions. Lots of intricate fine details suitable for close viewing, but a wide geological scale rather than a close-up slab.

Lighting: bright neutral diffuse daylight, materially brighter than the shadowed reference image 2. Palette: subdued warm rose-brown, sandstone beige, pale warm stone-gray and concentrated dark brown-gray beds. Strong local tonal contrast and real small-scale color detail, but overall saturation restrained to fit satellite terrain. No green, no orange photographic filter, no pure white or black. No baked cast shadows or sun highlights. Seamless square, edges wrap smoothly without a border. Entire image is continuous front-on rock, no ground/sky/landscape/vegetation/perspective/text. Photorealistic albedo texture. Maximum available resolution, ideally 4096x4096; keep all resolved fine detail sharp.

Edit this exact canyon rock texture with one targeted correction. Keep its composition, layer placement, uneven fine strata, cracks, broad dusty rose sandstone beds, dark weathered bands, overall palette and scale. The PALE THINLY LAMINATED intervals currently have far too much small-scale contrast, with white sharp highlights above almost black crevices, looking like extreme hard directional shadows. Remove that baked directional shading: reduce the fine light/dark relief contrast within those lighter strata substantially (roughly half), lift the narrow dark crevices there to medium warm stone tones, lower tiny glaring edges to soft beige. Preserve fine resolved color grain and subtle fracture definition; DO NOT blur or smear the rock texture. The lighter layers should look like softly lit diffuse stone albedo. Broad dark geological beds must remain dark and distinct; don't flatten contrast between different strata or erase the mineral variation in the thick rose beds. Neutral soft diffuse illumination everywhere, no cast shadows or specular highlights. Keep seamless wrap, full-frame rock, square format. Retain sharp small-scale details; output highest available resolution, ideally 4096x4096. No labels or borders.

Revise the first image (game cliff albedo); use second image (real cliff photo) to correct geological structure. Two problems must be fixed:
1. The pale intervals in image 1 look horizontally stretched, like smeared parallel ribbons or noodles. REPLACE those features with naturally proportioned angular stone fragments, short broken slabs, small equant block faces and branching fractures. Break horizontal continuity frequently with cross joints and chips. Absolutely no long thin embossed rope lines, warped flow lines, or horizontally stretched grain. Fine lamination exists but is discontinuous and rugged like the photograph.
2. The big layers start and stop as flat, abrupt uniform bands. Give their contacts natural local variety: ragged eroded boundaries of gently varying height, pinch-outs, thin interleaved beds, rubble pockets and gradual mineral staining across some contacts. Within each main interval, vary grain, sub-beds, local thickness and color. Keep a geological sequence with distinctly different lithologies up the image: dusty pale beige broken blocky beds, muted rose massive jointed beds, darker warm-gray/brown weathered beds and finer rusty/taupe sedimentary intervals. Avoid identical repeated pale/dark/rose triplets. Different intervals have different proportions and fine structure. Dark minerals concentrated in selected beds, not scattered uniformly over all layers. Do not make contacts perfectly straight stripes or soft horizontal airbrush gradients. Preserve strong but natural broad contrast, subdued warm mineral palette, visible small-scale color variation and soft diffuse albedo lighting. No hard baked shadows or white edge highlights.

Wide zoomed-out front view of one continuous canyon wall, many small fractures and grains, rough photorealistic stone at multiple scales. Entire square filled with material, not a scene. No sky, ground, plants, terraces receding in perspective, text or border. Tileable seamless all edges, normal undistorted proportions of rock grain. Maximum resolution possible.
